steps.title: Act where you are stronger
steps.source: In these cases the general rule is to act immediately on the side where you have the superior forces.

narration.say: Now there are pawns on both sides of the board.
On the queen side, one pawn each.
On the king side, White has two pawns against one. That is where White must act, immediately.

steps.title: Your turn: the first push
steps.source: It is generally advisable to advance the Pawn that is free from opposition.

narration.say: Your move. Remember the rule about the free pawn.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Start the king-side advance.

feedback.h4: The h-pawn has a black pawn in front of it. Push the free one.
feedback.h3: The h-pawn has a black pawn in front of it. Push the free one.
feedback.g3: Right pawn, but take two steps: there is no time to waste.
feedback.*: Act on the king side, where you are stronger.

exercise.hint: The g-pawn has no black pawn in front of it.
exercise.success: 1. g4. Black advances on the other side: a5.

steps.title: Stop the other pawn?
steps.source: In this case either way wins, but generally the advance should be stopped when the opposing King is far away.

narration.say: Should White stop the black pawn? Here either way wins.
But generally, stop the advance when the opposing king is far away. Your move.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Stop the black a-pawn.

feedback.*: Block the black pawn with your own a-pawn.

steps.title: The winning plan
steps.source: Now it is time to go to the other side with the King, win the Black Pawn and Queen the single Pawn. This is typical of all such endings.

narration.say: Pawn to h4. Black to e6.
Pawn to g5. Black to f7.
King to f5. Black to g7.
Pawn to h5. Black to f7.
King to e5. Now the two pawns defend each other, and the king is free.
It goes to the other side, wins the pawn on a5, and queens the a-pawn.
With pawns on both wings, act immediately where you have more pawns.
Stop the enemy pawn when his king is far away.
Then use your king to win on the other side.
